name: Light Tan
lede: Light Tan is a pale cream-yellow on screens, much lighter than the leather tan its name suggests, and it has a family of older names.

sections.title: A tan that is not tan
sections.body:
Our library's Light Tan swatch is a pale yellow, #FBEEAC [1]. Older charts file almost identical colors under other names: Vanilla, Martius Yellow, Pale Green-Yellow and Naphthalene Yellow, all within 2.5 units [1]. Their dates run from 1912 to 1925 in Maerz and Paul's dictionary [1]. For the darker, leathery color, see [[tan]].

The light tans of history were uniform colors. In St Clair's account, cavalry wore buff leather coats in the 1500s and 1600s, and by the mid-1700s buff breeches were standard for a well-dressed European gentleman [2]. Light tans stayed in military uniform through the nineteenth century, usually as a facing beside bolder colors such as emerald green and Prussian blue [2]. Compare [[buff]], [[khaki]] and [[cream]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 64 (0.27 per cent) hold a color within six units of this pale yellow over at least five per cent of the canvas [3]. The 1800s hold 38 of them, out of 8,345 works [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [3].
